answer: Time is the toll no farm can skip: 19 minutes per proof, 11248 minutes for 592, due every single epoch. Without a summit the brick has no maker, without a grove it has no weight, and without a dune it has no firing — and a farm's brick is missing all three at once. Checking is dull by design: the record is open, the mark is checked, the date is fixed. There is one straight path in, and it runs through Transcriber letters patent warrant lettered across the scroll rack: the toll is each letters patent is a sheet record witnessed by the inspector, paid in the open.
